results.original_statement_md:
Based on the propagation rule in frequency in Section 3, we discover a further counter-intuitive phenomenon, i.e., in the scenario of an auto-encoder, if salient frequency components in the input sample and salient frequency components in the target output for regression have a small shift, then the decoder usually cannot be effectively learned.

Let us consider the input $x\in\mathbb R^{M\times N}$ with a single channel to simplify the proof. Then, $G\in\mathbb C^{M\times N}$, $H\in\mathbb C^{M\times N}$, and $H^*\in\mathbb C^{M\times N}$ denote spectrums of the input, the output, and the target image to fit, respectively. In a traditional auto-encoder, people usually set the target image the same as the input image, thereby $H^*=G$. Whereas, let us slightly shift a salient frequency component $[u_1,v_1]$, which is denoted by $G_{u_1v_1}\in\mathbb C$, to its neighboring frequency $[u_2,v_2]$ to construct $H^*$ and obtain the target image. Because the frequency component $G_{u_1v_1}$ is salient, we can consider there is a significant increase of $|H^*_{u_2v_2}|$ and a significance decrease of $|H^*_{u_1v_1}|$, compared with the traditional setting of $H^*=G$. Thus, we apply the following setting as a typical case, which simplifies the analysis of the representation problem. That is, $H^*_{u_1v_1}=(1-A)G^{(u_1v_1)}$, and $H^*_{u_2v_2}=(1+\overline A)G^{(u_2v_2)}$, where $A=\alpha e^{i\varphi}$, and $\overline A$ denotes the conjugate of $A$; $\alpha>0$; $\varphi<\frac\pi2$. In this way, we can decrease the significance of $H^*_{u_1v_1}$ and increase the significance of $H^*_{u_2v_2}$.

According to Corollary 3.3, learning an identify function $H=G$ is not difficult for an auto-encoder, because we can just make $\forall u,v,\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}=I$. Thus, to investigate the extreme difficulty of learning specific frequencies, let us take the auto-encoder that models the identify function as the baseline network. Then, we further tune the auto-encoder to fit the image with a shifted spectrum $H^*$ and compute the weight changes $\Delta\mathbf W$ as the cost of network training. A large weight change $\|\Delta\mathbf W\|$ indicates the high difficulty of fitting $H^*$. Note that we must ensure that parameters $\mathbf W$ are real-valued, instead of being complex-valued, when we train the auto-encoder. Theorem 4.5 proves a case that $\mathbf W$ is optimized to satisfy $H_{u_1v_1}=H^*_{u_1v_1}$ and $H_{u_2v_2}=H^*_{u_2v_2}$ simultaneously.

Theorem 4.5. (Proof in Appendix A.7) Let us consider the objective function in the form $\lambda_1|H_{u_1v_1}-H^*_{u_1v_1}|^2+\lambda_2|H_{u_2v_2}-H^*_{u_2v_2}|^2$. We prove specific constrains of $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$, and $A$ that make the auto-encoder learnable (i.e., ensuring $\Delta\mathbf W$ is real-valued) and make the objective function can reach zero by a single step of gradient descent, which are shown in Equations (43) and (44) in Appendix A.7. Then, we prove the significance of the weight change $\Delta\mathbf W$, as follows.

$$\|\Delta\mathbf W\|\propto\frac{\alpha MN}{K^2-\frac{\sin(K(u_2-u_1)\pi/M)}{\sin((u_2-u_1)\pi/M)}\frac{\sin(K(v_2-v_1)\pi/N)}{\sin((v_2-v_1)\pi/N)}}.\tag{12}$$

We represent parameters of multiple layers as a vector.
results.original_proof_md:
In this section, we prove Theorem 4.5 in the main paper. Recall that we consider the input $x\in\mathbb R^{M\times N}$ with a single channel to simplify the proof. Then, $G\in\mathbb C^{M\times N}$, $H\in\mathbb C^{M\times N}$, and $H^*\in\mathbb C^{M\times N}$ denote spectrums of the input, the output, and the target image to fit, respectively. Specifically, $H^*_{u_1v_1}=(1-A)G^{(u_1v_1)}$, and $H^*_{u_2v_2}=(1+\overline A)G^{(u_2v_2)}$, where $A=\alpha e^{i\phi}$ and $\overline A$ denotes the conjugate of $A$; $\alpha>0$; $\phi<\pi/2$. Theorem 4.5 proves a case that weights $\mathbf W$ is optimized to satisfy $H_{u_1v_1}=H^*_{u_1v_1}$ and $H_{u_2v_2}=H^*_{u_2v_2}$ simultaneously.

Proof. Let us provide specific constrains as follows, so as to make the auto-encoder learnable (i.e., ensuring $\Delta\mathbf W$ is real-valued) and make the objective function can reach zero by a single step of gradient descent.

$$\lambda_1=\frac1{|G_{u_1v_1}|^2};\qquad\lambda_2=\frac1{|G_{u_2v_2}|^2}.\tag{43}$$

$$A=\alpha e^{i\phi},\qquad\text{s.t. }\phi=\left(\frac{(K-1)(u_2-u_1)}M+\frac{(K-1)(v_2-v_1)}N\right)\frac\pi2.\tag{44}$$

$$\mathbb T^{(u_2v_2)(L:1)}=\mathbb T^{(u_1v_1)(L:1)}=1.\tag{45}$$

$$\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(u_1v_1)(L:l+1)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(u_1v_1)(l-1:1)}\|^2=\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(u_2v_2)(L:l+1)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(u_2v_2)(l-1:1)}\|^2.\tag{46}$$

If the objective function can reach zero (i.e., $H_{u_1v_1}=H^*_{u_1v_1}$ and $H_{u_2v_2}=H^*_{u_2v_2}$) by a single step of gradient descent, the change of weights $\Delta\mathbf W$ can be rewritten as $\eta\frac{Loss}{\partial\mathbf W}$, where $\eta$ denotes the learning rate, $\frac{Loss}{\partial\mathbf W}$ denotes the gradient on weights. Then, we will prove the formulations of $\eta$ and $\|\frac{Loss}{\partial\mathbf W}\|$.

According to Corollary 3.3, the network output $H_{uv}$ can be computed as follows.

$$H_{uv}=\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}G_{uv},\tag{47}$$

where $\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}=T^{(L,uv)}T^{(L-1,uv)}\cdots T^{(1,uv)}\in\mathbb C^{1\times1}$.

According to Corollary 3.4, after a single step of gradient descent, the change of $\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}$ can be computed as follows.

$$\begin{aligned}
\Delta\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}
&=\Delta(T^{(L,uv)}T^{(L-1,uv)}\cdots T^{(1,uv)})\\
&\approx\sum_{l=1}^L\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(uv)}\Delta T^{(l,uv)}\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(uv)}\quad\text{//First order approximation}\\
&=-\eta MN\sum_{l=1}^L\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(uv)}\left(\sum_{u'v'}\chi_{u'v'uv}\overline{\mathbb T}^{(l-1:1)(uv)}\overline G_{uv}\frac{\partial Loss}{\partial\overline H^T_{uv}}\overline{\mathbb T}^{(L:l-1)(uv)}\right)^T\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(uv)}\\
&=-2\eta MN\left(\lambda_1\chi_{u_1v_1uv}\overline G_{u_1v_1}(H_{u_1v_1}-H^*_{u_1v_1})+\lambda_2\chi_{u_2v_2uv}\overline G_{u_2v_2}(H_{u_2v_2}-H^*_{u_2v_2})\right)\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(uv)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(uv)}\|^2\\
&=-2\eta MN\left(\chi_{u_1v_1uv}\left(\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_1v_1)}-\frac{H^*_{u_1v_1}}{G_{u_1v_1}}\right)+\chi_{u_2v_2uv}\left(\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_2v_2)}-\frac{H^*_{u_2v_2}}{G_{u_2v_2}}\right)\right)\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(uv)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(uv)}\|^2\quad\text{//According to Equation (43)}\\
&=-2\eta MN(A\chi_{u_1v_1uv}-\overline A\chi_{u_2v_2uv})\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(uv)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(uv)}\|^2\quad\text{//Equation (45)}.
\end{aligned}\tag{48}$$

For frequencies $[u_1,v_1]$ and $[u_2,v_2]$, we have:

$$\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_1v_1)}=-2\eta MN(A\chi_{u_1v_1u_1v_1}-\overline A\chi_{u_2v_2u_1v_1})\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(u_1v_1)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(u_1v_1)}\|^2.\tag{49}$$

$$\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_2v_2)}=-2\eta MN(A\chi_{u_1v_1u_2v_2}-\overline A\chi_{u_2v_2u_2v_2})\sum_{l=1}^L\|\mathbb T^{(L:l+1)(u_2v_2)}\|^2\|\mathbb T^{(l-1:1)(u_2v_2)}\|^2.\tag{50}$$

en.overview: Every DFT of the delta input is one, so both λ values in (43) are one. Equation (44) gives phase $[(1)(1)/4+(1)(-1)/4]\pi/2=0$. Identity kernels have unit response, so (45) has product one and both bypass-norm sums in (46) are two. α=1/4 also gives the intended decrease/increase.

assumptions.body_md: Source Assumption 3.1 uses stride one, positive-offset convolution and circular padding preserving $M\times N$. The activation-free linear cascade may have varying channel widths.
M=N=4,K=2,L=2, one channel, identity delta kernels, zero biases and delta input. Let f1=(0,1), f2=(1,0), α=1/4 and φ=0, with the original loss using only the two selected frequencies.

definitions.body_md: The output DFT has negative phase, $\widehat f(u,v)=\sum_{m,n}f_{mn}e^{-2\pi i(um/M+vn/N)}$, while the kernel response has positive phase, $T_{dc}^{(uv)}=\sum_{t,s}W_{cts}^{[\mathrm{ker}=d]}e^{2\pi i(ut/M+vs/N)}$.

Keep $\mathbb T^{(uv)(b:a)}=T^{(b,uv)}\cdots T^{(a,uv)}$ in its original order, with empty layer products equal to identity maps, and $\delta_{uv}=1_{\{u=v=0\}}$. Retain spatial biases $b^{(l)}$; spectral bias acts only at DC and carries $MN$.

The finite sums $P_K(z)=\sum_{t<K}z^t$, $R_{uv}=\sum_{t,s<K}e^{2\pi i(ut/M+vs/N)}$, and $\chi_{u^{\prime}v^{\prime}uv}=(MN)^{-1}R_{u-u^{\prime},v-v^{\prime}}$ include equal-coordinate frequencies, with $\chi_{uvuv}=K^2/(MN)$.

The target has values 1−α and 1+α at the selected frequencies, their conjugates at negative frequencies, and one elsewhere. Hermitian inverse DFT yields a real target image without adding conjugate terms to the loss.

For any other frequency component $[u,v]$, where $u\ne u_1$, $u\ne u_2$, $v\ne v_1$, $v\ne v_2$, the change $\Delta\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}$ can be cpmputed as the linear combination of the $\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_1v_1)}$ and $\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_2v_2)}$ as follows.

$$\Delta\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}=a_1\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_1v_1)}+a_2\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_2v_2)}.\tag{51}$$

where $a_1\in\mathbb C$ and $a_2\in\mathbb C$ are two complex coefficients, which keep unchanged during the learning process.

On the other hand, the exact change of $\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}$ can be directly computed given the objective function. For frequencies $[u_1,v_1]$ and $[u_2,v_2]$, we have:

$$\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_1v_1)}=\frac{H^*_{u_1v_1}}{G_{u_1v_1}}-\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_1v_1)}=-A.\tag{52}$$

$$\Delta\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_2v_2)}=\frac{H^*_{u_2v_2}}{G_{u_2v_2}}-\mathbb T^{(L:1)(u_2v_2)}=\overline A.\tag{53}$$

For any other frequency component $[u,v]$, the change $\Delta\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}$ can be computed as follows:

$$\Delta\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)}=-a_1A+a_2\overline A.\tag{54}$$

Then, combining Equation (51) and Equation (54), we can obtain the value of $\eta$.

\eta&\propto\frac{-a_1A+a_2\overline A}{-a_1(A\chi_{u_1v_1u_1v_1}-\overline A\chi_{u_2v_2u_1v_1})-a_2(A\chi_{u_1v_1u_2v_2}-\overline A\chi_{u_2v_2u_2v_2})}\quad\text{//Equation (46)}\\

&=\frac{-a_1A+a_2\overline A}{-a_1A+a_2\overline A}\cdot\frac{MN}{K^2-\dfrac{\sin(K(u_2-u_1)\pi/M)\sin(K(v_2-v_1)\pi/N)}{\sin((u_2-u_1)\pi/M)\sin((v_2-v_1)\pi/N)}}\\
&=\frac{MN}{K^2-\dfrac{\sin(K(u_2-u_1)\pi/M)\sin(K(v_2-v_1)\pi/N)}{\sin((u_2-u_1)\pi/M)\sin((v_2-v_1)\pi/N)}}.
\end{aligned}\tag{55}$$

Theorem 4.4 shows that the upsampling operation repeats the strong magnitude of the fundamental frequency $G^{(c)}_{00}$ of the lower layer to different frequency components $\forall c,H^{(c)}_{u^*v^*}$ of the higher layer, where $u^*=0,M_0,2M_0,\ldots$; $v^*=0,N_0,2N_0,\ldots$. (Conclusion) The upsampling operation makes the upconvolution operation generate a feature spectrum, in which strong signals of the input periodically appear at certain frequencies. Such strong periodic signals hurt the representation capacity of the network.

More crucially, according to the spectrum propagation in Corollary 3.3, such periodic frequency components can be further propagated to upper layers. Thus, Corollary 3.3 may provide some clues to differentiate real samples and the generated samples.

results.original_statement_md:
If the cascaded convolutional decoder network is trained on natural images, then the decoder network is less likely to learn high-frequency components.

Verifying factors that strengthened low-frequency components. Previous studies (Ruderman, 1994) have empirically found that natural images were dominated by low-frequency components.
results.original_proof_md:
If the cascaded convolutional decoder network is trained on natural images, then the decoder network is less likely to learn high-frequency components. Previous studies (Ruderman, 1994) have empirically found that natural images were dominated by low-frequency components. Specifically, frequency spectrums of natural images follow a Power-law distribution. I.e., low-frequency components (e.g., the frequency component $[u,v]$ closed to $[0,0]$, $[0,N-1]$, $[M-1,0]$, and $[M-1,N-1]$) have much larger length $\|\mathbf g^{(uv)}\|_2=\sqrt{\sum_c|G^{(c)}_{uv}|^2}$ than other frequency components. Besides, according to rules of the forward propagation in Equation (4) and the change of $T^{(l,uv)}$ in Equation (5), if the frequency component $\mathbf g^{(uv)}$ of the input image has a large magnitude, then $\mathbf h^{(uv)}$ of the output image also has a large magnitude. This means that using natural images as the input strengthens the trend of encoding low-frequency components.

Therefore, according to Corollaries 3.3 and 3.4, we know that if the cascaded convolutional decoder is trained on natural images, then the decoder is more likely to strengthen low-frequencies. Please see Appendix B.4 for more discussions. Besides, we conducted experiments to verify the following three factors that were found to strengthen low frequencies.

results.original_statement_md:
C.6. Discussions on the curse of dimension

In this section, we discuss the problem of the curse of dimension, when we compute the cosine similarity of two high-dimensional vectors with as many as $32^2$, $64^2$ or $224^2$ dimensions. In general, for each pair of extremely high-dimensional vectors, it's hard for these vectors to have very high cosine similarity.
results.original_proof_md: It is because even if the noisy differences between many pairs of dimensions can be ignored, in the process of calculating the sum of squares, these noisy differences will accumulate. Therefore, the cosine similarity of two extremely high-dimensional vectors will not be particularly large.

results.original_statement_md:
C.7. Verifying that Assumption 3.1 can be applied to fully trained DNNs

Assumption 4.1 shows that in early training of a DNN, all elements in $T^{(l,uv)}$ are irrelevant to each other, and $\forall l\ne l'$, elements in $T^{(l,uv)}$ and $T^{(l',uv)}$ are irrelevant to each other. In this section, we further conducted experiments to verify that such irrelevant relationships also existed in a fully trained DNN. To this end, we constructed a cascaded convolutional auto-encoder by using the VGG-16 as the encoder network. The decoder network contained ten convolutional layers, where the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th layers were traditional convolutional layers, and the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, and 10th layers were upconvolutional layers. Each convolutional/upconvolutional layer applied zero-paddings and was followed by a batch normalization layer and an ReLU layer. The network was trained on the Tiny-ImageNet dataset using the mean squared error (MSE) loss for image reconstruction.
results.original_proof_md:
Let the above auto-encoder be trained to convergence. Then, we computed the Pearson's correlation coefficient between each random pair of variables $|\Delta T_{d_1c_1}^{(l,uv)}|$ and $|\Delta T_{d_2c_2}^{(l,uv)}|$ through different images, denoted by $r(|\Delta T_{d_1c_1}^{(l,uv)}|,|\Delta T_{d_2c_2}^{(l,uv)}|)$, to measure the relevance between two elements $T_{d_1c_1}^{(l,uv)}$ and $T_{d_2c_2}^{(l,uv)}$ in $T^{(l,uv)}$. Here, $\Delta T^{(l,uv)}$ denoted the change of $T^{(l,uv)}$ when we updated parameters $\mathbf W$ for a single gradient-descent step on a single input sample. Results in Table 1 show that even when the network was fully trained, different elements in $T^{(l,uv)}$ had low Pearson's correlation coefficient $r$. This proved that our assumption that all elements in $T^{(l,uv)}$ were irrelevant to each other was reasonable. The last three convolutional layers in the decoder showed a larger Pearson's correlation coefficient, because network parameters close to the output layer had been converged to the principle feature direction of each category. Nevertheless, our experiments showed that for most layers, we could keep Assumption 4.1, which enabled to us to prove that convolution operations in these layers weakened high-frequency components.

results.original_statement_md:
Previous studies (Tse & Viswanath, 2005) proved that given $N$ complex numbers, if each complex number follows a Gaussian distribution, then the linear summation of these $N$ complex numbers also follows a Gaussian distribution of complex numbers.

If the decoder network is deep, then the decoder network is less likely to learn high-frequency components. It is because $|R_{uv}|$ is relatively large for low-frequency components. In this way, the large effect of a single layer's $T^{(l,uv)}$ of low-frequency components on $\log\operatorname{SOM}(\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)})$, i.e., $\log(|\mu_lR_{uv}|^2+K^2\sigma_l^2)$, can be accumulated through different layers according to (1) the Law of Large Numbers, and (2) the independent effects $\log(|\mu_lR_{uv}|^2+K^2\sigma_l^2)$ between different layers' $T^{(l,uv)}$ on $\log\operatorname{SOM}(\mathbb T^{(uv)(L:1)})=\sum_{l=1}^L\log(|\mu_lR_{uv}|^2+K^2\sigma_l^2)$.

Therefore, the large $|R_{u^{\mathrm{low}}v^{\mathrm{low}}}|$ value for a low-frequency component $[u^{\mathrm{low}},v^{\mathrm{low}}]$ makes $\mathbb T^{(u^{\mathrm{low}}v^{\mathrm{low}})(L:1)}$ more likely to have a large norm, whereas the small $|R_{u^{\mathrm{high}}v^{\mathrm{high}}}|$ value for a high-frequency component $[u^{\mathrm{high}},v^{\mathrm{high}}]$ makes $\mathbb T^{(u^{\mathrm{high}}v^{\mathrm{high}})(L:1)}$ less likely to have a large norm. This indicates that a deep decoder network will almost certainly strengthen the encoding of low-frequency components of the input sample, while weaken the encoding of high-frequency components.

results.original_statement_md:
3.2. Experimental verification of Corollaries 3.3 and 3.4

To verify the correctness of Corollary 3.3, we computed the similarity between real spectrums $\mathbf H^*=[H^{*(1)},H^{*(2)},\ldots]$ measured by applying the DFT to the real network output, and spectrums $\mathbf H=[H^{(1)},H^{(2)},\ldots]$ derived in Corollary 3.3. Specifically, we measured the cosine similarity $sim(\mathbf H^*,\mathbf H)=\mathbb E_c[\mathbf{cos}(\mathbf{vec}(mag(H^{*(c)})),\mathbf{vec}(mag(H^{(c)})))]$, where $\mathbf{vec}(\cdot)$ represented the vectorization of a matrix, and $mag(\cdot)$ transferred a complex-valued matrix to a real-valued magnitude matrix.

The function $B=mag(A)$ returns a matrix, where each element $B_{ij}\in\mathbb R$ represents the magnitude of $A_{ij}\in\mathbb C$.

To this end, we constructed the following three baseline networks to verify whether Corollary 3.3 derived from specific assumptions could also objectively reflect real forward propagations in real neural networks. The first baseline network contained 10 convolutional layers. Each convolutional layer applied zero-paddings and was followed by an ReLU layer. Each convolutional layer contained 16 convolutional kernels (kernel size was $3\times3$) with 16 bias terms. We set the stride size of the convolution operation to 1. The second baseline network was constructed by removing all ReLU layers from the first baseline network, which was closer to the assumption in Corollary 3.3. The third baseline network was revised from the second baseline network by replacing all zero-paddings with circular paddings. The third baseline network followed the exact assumption in Corollary 3.3.

Figure 3(a) reports $sim(\mathbf H^*,\mathbf H)$ that was measured on spectrums in different layers and averaged over all samples. The similarity between real spectrums and derived spectrums was large for all the three baseline networks, which verified Corollary 3.3. Note that the cosine similarity was computed based on high-dimensional vectors with as many as $32^2$, $64^2$ or $224^2$ dimensions (determined by the dataset). For such high-dimensional vectors, a similarity greater than 0.8 was already significant enough to verify the practicality of our theory.

Please see Appendix C.6 for the curse of dimension.

Besides, in order to verify Corollary 3.4, we also measured the similarity between the real change of $T^{(l,uv)}$ computed by measuring real network parameters, termed $\Delta^*T^{(l,uv)}$, and the change of $T^{(l,uv)}$ derived with assumptions in Corollary 3.4, termed $\Delta T^{(l,uv)}$. The similarity was also computed as $sim(\Delta^*T^{(l,uv)},\Delta T^{(l,uv)})=\mathbb E_c[\mathbf{cos}(\mathbf{vec}(mag(\Delta^*T^{(l,uv)})),\mathbf{vec}(mag(\Delta T^{(l,uv)})))]$. The verification was also conducted on the above three baseline networks. Figure 3(b) reports $\forall l,sim(\Delta^*T^{(l,uv)},\Delta T^{(l,uv)})$ averaged over all samples. The similarity was greater than 0.88 for all three baseline networks, which was large enough to verify Corollary 3.4.

(3) Verifying that a small kernel size $K$ strengthened low-frequency components. To this end, we compared feature spectrums of networks with different kernel sizes. Therefore, we constructed three networks with kernel sizes of $1\times1$, $3\times3$, and $5\times5$. Each network contained 5 convolutional layers, each layer contained 16 convolutional kernels, except for the last layer containing 3 kernels. We used the metric

$$p^{\mathrm{low}}=\frac{\sum_{[u,v]\in\Omega^{\mathrm{low}}}\mathbb E_c[|H_{uv}^{(c)}|^2]}{\sum_{uv}\mathbb E_c[|H_{uv}^{(c)}|^2]}$$

to measure the ratio of low-frequency components to all frequencies, where $\Omega^{\mathrm{low}}$ denoted the set of low-frequency components. Figure 4(d) reports the average $p^{\mathrm{low}}$ value over all images. Results show that the network with a small kernel size encoded more low-frequency components.

Low-frequencies $[u,v]\in\Omega^{\mathrm{low}}$ were included in $u\in\{u\mid0\le u<M/8\}\cup\{u\mid7M/8\le u<M\}$ and $v\in\{v\mid0\le v<N/8\}\cup\{v\mid7N/8\le v<N\}$.

We used the metric

$$\Delta x_{mn}=\left\|[x_{mn}^{*(1)},x_{mn}^{*(2)},\ldots,x_{mn}^{*(C)}]-[\hat x_{mn}^{(1)},\hat x_{mn}^{(2)},\ldots,\hat x_{mn}^{(C)}]\right\|_2$$

to measure the fitting error on the pixel $[m,n]$ between the target output $x^*\in\mathbb R^{C\times M\times N}$ and the network output $\hat x\in\mathbb R^{C\times M\times N}$. Figure 1(c) shows the heatmap of the fitting error $\Delta x_{mn}$, and the histogram of fitting errors $|\Delta x_{mn}|$ over different pixels. Results show that when the target frequency components were shifted by a smaller distance, it was more difficult to learn a decoder to fit the target image, i.e., yielding larger fitting errors in Figure 1(c.1,c.2). Besides, Figure 1(c.3) reports the average weight change $\|\Delta\mathbf W\|$ over different DNNs, which was decreased along with the shifting distance. This also verified that it took more effort to learn a decoder to fit the target image, when the target frequency components were shifted by a smaller distance.

C.10. More experimental details

assumptions.text_md: S 是有限变量集合。g 与 d 是定义在有限变量子集上的任意实值函数；不要求连续、可微、独立性或零输出基线。
U 表示变量总体，\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(U)\) 表示其所有有限子集。每次参与求和的 S、T 都有限；变量总体本身可以无限。论文应用则固定有限总体 N，只讨论 \(2^N\)。

definitions.text_md: 交互是有限交替和。\(T\subseteq S\) 保证 |T|≤|S|，因此指数 \(|S|-|T|\) 是非负整数。
\(R_d\) 是在给定保留变量集 S 上累加所有被激活的系数。
插入差分比较保留 i 与掩码 i 两种状态。下面的插入引理只在 \(i\notin S\) 时使用。

shared_proofs.overview: 每次插入新变量 $i$，把子集分成含 $i$ 与不含 $i$ 两类。含 $i$ 的交互等于插入差分的交互；对两类分别应用加强归纳假设，中间输出相消，留下当前输出。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：为什么子集能分成两组
proof_steps.body_md: 固定有限集合 S 及不属于 S 的变量 i。\(S\cup \{i\}\) 的任何子集 A，要么不含 i，这时 A 本身就是 S 的子集；要么含 i，这时唯一地写成 \(A=T\cup \{i\}\)，其中 \(T=A\setminus \{i\}\subseteq S\)。两类互不重叠，且各自覆盖所有可能情况，所以对任意实值函数 F 可以把有限和改写为下面的两组和。没有遗漏空集：它出现在第一组 \(T=\varnothing\)；第二组 \(T=\varnothing\) 对应 {i}。
proof_steps.justification: 子集与不含/含 i 两类的显式一一对应。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 插入引理证明内实际使用子集拆分；这一步没有另增一个项目定理。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：展开符号，得到插入差分
proof_steps.body_md: 把上一步用于交互 \(I_g(S\cup \{i\})\) 的定义。每个 \(T\subseteq S\) 都满足 \(i\notin T\)，因此 \(|S\cup \{i\}|=|S|+1\)、\(|T\cup \{i\}|=|T|+1\)。令 \(k=|S|-|T|\ge 0\)：第一组的系数是 \((-1)^{k+1}=-(-1)^k\)；第二组的系数是 \((-1)^k\)。把同一 T 的两项合并，得到 \((-1)^k\)[\(g(T\cup \{i\})−g(T)\)]。最后一行正是 \(I_{\Delta_i g}(S)\) 的定义。
proof_steps.justification: \(i\notin S\) 及 \(T\subseteq S\) 给出两个插入基数；整数幂的递推关系给出负号；有限和逐项相加。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：加强归纳命题，并处理空集
proof_steps.body_md:
对有限集合 S 作插入归纳，但归纳命题必须说“对任意集合函数 g 都有 \(R_{I_g}(S)=g(S)\)”。不能只固定最初的 g 后归纳，因为插入一步还要对新函数 \(\Delta_i g\) 使用归纳假设。

当 \(S=\varnothing\) 时，空集只有一个子集，即自身。定义中的指数是 0，(−1)^0=1，所以 \(I_g(\varnothing )=g(\varnothing )\)，而重构和也只有这一项。这是归纳起点；无需且不能在这里默默令 \(g(\varnothing )\)=0。
proof_steps.justification: 有限集合插入归纳；空集的子集族只有空集本身；空集交互公式。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 归纳语句 generalizing v 以及 empty 分支都在 reconstruction 的现有证明内。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：对两组和分别使用归纳假设
proof_steps.body_md: 现在设 \(i\notin S\)，并假设任意函数 h 在 S 上都满足 \(R_{I_h}(S)\)=h(S)。第一步的拆分把 \(S\cup \{i\}\) 上的重构和写成两组。对第二组中的每个 \(T\subseteq S\)，仍有 \(i\notin T\)，所以第二步的插入交互引理可以逐项使用。得到的第二组是 \(\Delta_i g\) 在 S 上的交互总和。对第一组用归纳假设 h=g，对第二组用归纳假设 h=\(\Delta_i g\)，便分别得到 \(g(S)\) 与 \(\Delta_i g(S)\)。这里明确使用了两次同一个归纳假设，而不是假设差分的结论未经证明成立。
proof_steps.justification: 子集拆分；插入交互引理逐项使用；加强归纳假设适用于任意集合函数。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 现有代码的 sum_congr、ih v 和 ih (marginal v i) 分别实现逐项替换和两次归纳应用。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：消去中间输出，完成归纳
proof_steps.body_md: 按插入差分的定义，\(\Delta_i g(S)=g(S\cup \{i\})-g(S)\)。将其代入上一步，\(g(S)\) 与 −\(g(S)\) 在实数加法中消去，得到所需的 \(g(S\cup \{i\})\)。空集起点与每次插入的步骤已经覆盖所有有限 S，因此对任意有限 S 的重构恒等式成立。论文中只需把这里的 \(g(S)\) 换成固定模型和掩码规则给出的 \(v(x_S)\)。
proof_steps.justification: 插入差分定义与实数加减法；有限集合归纳结论。

lean.adapter_code:
theorem interaction_insert (v : Game α) (S : Finset α) (i : α) (hi : i ∉ S) :
    interaction v (insert i S) = interaction (marginal v i) S := by
  unfold interaction marginal
  rw [sum_powerset_insert hi]
  have h1 : ∀ T ∈ S.powerset,
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ ((insert i S).card - T.card) * v T =
      -((-1 : ℝ) ^ (S.card - T.card) * v T) := by
    intro T hT
    have hTS := card_le_card (mem_powerset.mp hT)
    rw [card_insert_of_notMem hi]
    have he : S.card + 1 - T.card = (S.card - T.card) + 1 := by omega
    rw [he, pow_succ]
    ring
  have h2 : ∀ T ∈ S.powerset,
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ ((insert i S).card - (insert i T).card) * v (insert i T) =
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ (S.card - T.card) * v (insert i T) := by
    intro T hT
    have hiT : i ∉ T := fun hit => hi ((mem_powerset.mp hT) hit)
    rw [card_insert_of_notMem hi, card_insert_of_notMem hiT]
    simp
  rw [sum_congr rfl h1, sum_congr rfl h2, ← sum_add_distrib]
  apply sum_congr rfl
  intro T _
  ring

/-- All dividends reconstruct every finite coalition, without a baseline assumption. -/

theorem reconstruction (v : Game α) (S : Finset α) :
    reconstruct (interaction v) S = v S := by
  induction S using Finset.induction_on generalizing v with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert i S hi ih =>
    unfold reconstruct
    rw [sum_powerset_insert hi]
    have h : ∀ T ∈ S.powerset,
        interaction v (insert i T) = interaction (marginal v i) T := by
      intro T hT
      exact interaction_insert v T i (fun hit => hi ((mem_powerset.mp hT) hit))
    rw [sum_congr rfl h]
    change reconstruct (interaction v) S + reconstruct (interaction (marginal v i)) S = _
    rw [ih v, ih (marginal v i)]
    simp [marginal]

/-- The converse Boolean Möbius inversion: transforming subset sums recovers coefficients. -/

en.title: Shared proof: exact reconstruction of every masked output

assumptions.text_md: The coalition is finite. The games and coefficient functions are arbitrary real-valued functions on finite subsets; continuity, differentiability, independence and a zero output baseline are unnecessary.
The ambient universe may be infinite, but every coalition in a sum is finite. Paper applications fix a finite universe and use its powerset.

definitions.text_md: The interaction is a finite alternating sum. Since the summation subset is contained in the target, the cardinality difference in its exponent is a nonnegative integer.
Reconstruction sums all coefficients activated by the retained-variable set.
The insertion difference compares retaining the distinguished variable with masking it. The insertion lemma below is used only when that variable is absent from the target.

en.overview: Insertion separates subsets with and without the new variable. The insertion interaction becomes a finite difference; strengthened induction reconstructs both games and cancels the intermediate output.
en.completion_scope: The public finite-set reconstruction theorem and its actual library induction; paper specializations are separate.
en.example_md: For two variables with mask outputs 2, 5, 7 and 13, the dividends are 2, 3, 5 and 3. Their full sum is 13, the empty-mask sum is 2, and singleton reconstruction gives 5 and 7. If only the full output 13 were required, coefficients 0, 0, 0 and 13 would also fit that one mask but fail all others. Hence the universal mask requirement matters.
caveats: The human proof explains the existing library declarations; its five steps do not introduce five new Lean theorems. The checked scope consists of the library theorem and separately compiled paper adapters.
Every subset sum includes the empty coefficient. If it is omitted, add the output baseline outside the sum.

The source uses double sums and binomial cancellation; the library uses insertion induction or converse inversion. These are separately identified proof routes, not a claim of line-by-line formal translation.

proof_steps.title: Partition the subsets into two families
proof_steps.body_md: Fix finite $S$ and $i\notin S$. Every subset of $S\cup\{i\}$ either excludes $i$, and is a subset $T$ of $S$, or includes $i$, and uniquely equals $T\cup\{i\}$ with $T\subseteq S$. The families are disjoint and exhaustive, so any finite sum of a function $F$ splits into these two sums. The empty subset occurs in the first family; empty $T$ in the second family produces $\{i\}$.
proof_steps.justification: The explicit bijections for subsets with and without the inserted variable.

proof_steps.title: Expand the signs to obtain the insertion difference
proof_steps.body_md: Every $T\subseteq S$ excludes $i$, so the two inserted cardinalities are $|S|+1$ and $|T|+1$. Put $k=|S|-|T|\ge0$. The coefficient of $g(T)$ is $(-1)^{k+1}=-(-1)^k$, and the coefficient of $g(T\cup\{i\})$ is $(-1)^k$. Combining the paired terms gives $(-1)^k[g(T\cup\{i\})-g(T)]$. The resulting sum is the interaction of $\Delta_i g$ on $S$.
proof_steps.justification: Insertion cardinalities, the recurrence for integer powers, and finite distributivity.

proof_steps.title: Strengthen the induction statement and handle the empty set
proof_steps.body_md: Induct by inserting elements into finite $S$, with the strengthened statement that reconstruction holds for every game $g$. This quantification is necessary because the next step applies induction to the new game $\Delta_i g$. When $S=\varnothing$, its only subset is itself; the exponent is zero, so both interaction and reconstruction equal $g(\varnothing)$. No zero-baseline assumption is used.
proof_steps.justification: Finite-set insertion induction and the exact empty-interaction formula.

proof_steps.title: Apply induction to each of the two sums
proof_steps.body_md: Assume that every game $h$ is reconstructed on $S$, and let $i\notin S$. Split the reconstruction on $S\cup\{i\}$ into the two families from the first step. In the family containing $i$, each $T\subseteq S$ still excludes $i$, so apply the insertion-difference identity term by term. The two sums become reconstruction for $g$ and reconstruction for $\Delta_i g$ on $S$. The same strengthened induction hypothesis gives $g(S)$ and $\Delta_i g(S)$ respectively.
proof_steps.justification: Subset partition, the insertion identity, and induction quantified over all games.

proof_steps.title: Cancel the intermediate output and finish induction
proof_steps.body_md: By definition, $\Delta_i g(S)=g(S\cup\{i\})-g(S)$. Adding it to $g(S)$ cancels the intermediate value and leaves the required output on the inserted set. The empty case and insertion step cover every finite set. For a paper application, instantiate the game with $g(S)=v(x_S)$ using one fixed model, input and mask rule.
proof_steps.justification: The finite-difference definition and real addition and subtraction.

shared_proofs.title: 公共证明：同时重构所有掩码输出的系数唯一

assumptions.text_md: S 是有限变量集合。g 与 d 是定义在有限变量子集上的任意实值函数；不要求连续、可微、独立性或零输出基线。
U 表示变量总体，\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(U)\) 表示其所有有限子集。每次参与求和的 S、T 都有限；变量总体本身可以无限。论文应用则固定有限总体 N，只讨论 \(2^N\)。
同一组系数 d 必须重构定义域内每一个有限子集的输出，包括空集。只在一个指定集合上重构不够。

definitions.text_md: 交互是有限交替和。\(T\subseteq S\) 保证 |T|≤|S|，因此指数 \(|S|-|T|\) 是非负整数。
\(R_d\) 是在给定保留变量集 S 上累加所有被激活的系数。
插入差分比较保留 i 与掩码 i 两种状态。下面的插入引理只在 \(i\notin S\) 时使用。

shared_proofs.overview: 把“对系数求子集和”再做一次交替差分，会恢复原系数。这是逆向 Möbius 反演 \(I_{R_d}=d\)。先证明这个辅助结论，再把“所有掩码上 \(R_d=g\)”的假设代入，就得到 \(d=I_g\)。下面完整证明所需的逆向反演，给出唯一性成立的理由。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：逆向反演的归纳起点
proof_steps.body_md:
先暂时不使用 \(R_d=g\)，单独证明任意系数函数 d 都满足 \(I_{R_d}(S)=d(S)\)。同样对有限 S 插入归纳，并把 d 保留为任意函数，因为插入步骤会引入新函数 e。

若 \(S=\varnothing\)，则 \(R_d(\varnothing )=d(\varnothing )\)。再由空集交互等于被变换函数的空集值，得 \(I_{R_d}(\varnothing )=R_d(\varnothing )=d(\varnothing )\)。这是逆向反演的起点，也说明空集系数并非可以随意选择的额外自由参数。
proof_steps.justification: 重构定义、空集交互公式与加强归纳。

lean_refs.explanation_md: interaction_reconstruct 对 S 归纳并 generalizing d；这一步为其 empty 分支。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：重构函数的差分也是一个重构
proof_steps.body_md:
设 \(i\notin S\)，并定义新的系数函数 \(e(U)=d(U\cup \{i\})\)。对任意 \(T\subseteq S\)，都有 \(i\notin T\)，可将 \(R_d(T\cup \{i\})\) 按不含/含 i 的子集拆成 \(R_d(T)\) 加 \(\sum _{U\subseteq T}d(U\cup \{i\})\)。减去 \(R_d(T)\) 后，留下的恰好是 \(R_e(T)\)。

注意该等式只在 \(T\subseteq S\) 的范围使用。若 T 已含 i，子集拆分就不再是两类互不重叠；这个局部等式不需要、也不能强行推广到不受 \(T\subseteq S\) 限制的每个 T。
proof_steps.formula_tex: \begin{aligned}(\Delta_i R_d)(T)&=R_d(T\cup\{i\})-R_d(T)\\&=\left(\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U)+\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U\cup\{i\})\right)-\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U)\\&=\sum_{U\subseteq T}e(U)=R_e(T),\qquad T\subseteq S.\end{aligned}
proof_steps.justification: \(i\notin T\)；子集拆分；相同有限和消去；e 与 \(R_e\) 的定义。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 库证明中的局部 h 使用 sum_powerset_insert；e 在代码中是 fun T => d (insert i T)。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：从局部一致性完成插入步骤
proof_steps.body_md: 先用重构证明中的插入交互引理，得到 \(I_{R_d}(S\cup \{i\})=I_{\Delta_i R_d}(S)\)。交互 \(I_h(S)\) 只读取 h 在 S 的子集上的值；第二步已经逐个证明 \(\Delta_i R_d(T)=R_e(T)\)，故两种函数在这次交替和中的每一项相同。因此 \(I_{\Delta_i R_d}(S)=I_{R_e}(S)\)。最后用“对任意系数函数”的归纳假设，将 \(I_{R_e}(S)\) 化为 \(e(S)=d(S\cup \{i\})\)。这样证明了逆向反演在插入集合上的结论。
proof_steps.justification: 插入交互引理；交互对参与求和的局部函数值保持一致；加强归纳假设。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 这里只要求在 S 的所有子集上相同，不要求两函数处处相同。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：将全部掩码的重构假设代入
proof_steps.body_md: 现在恢复假设 ∀T，\(R_d(T)=g(T)\)。固定任意 S。由刚证完的逆向反演，\(d(S)=I_{R_d}(S)\)。在定义 \(I_{R_d}(S)\) 的有限和中，每个 U 都满足 \(U\subseteq S\)，重构假设给出 \(R_d(U)=g(U)\)。逐项替换后，该和就是 \(I_g(S)\)。因此 \(d(S)=I_g(S)\)。这一步使用的是同一组 d 在所有掩码上的假设，而不是每个 S 临时选一组系数。
proof_steps.justification: 逆向反演与逐个子集上的重构假设。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：逐点相等与适用范围
proof_steps.body_md:
S 是任意有限子集，所以 d 与 \(I_g\) 在定义域的每个输入上取相同值，这正是两个函数相等的含义。本公共命题的量词遍历 U 的所有有限子集；应用于论文时把总体固定为有限 N，函数定义域随之取为 \(2^N\)。

特别取 \(S=\varnothing\)，重构假设强制 \(d(\varnothing )=g(\varnothing )\)。取 \(S=\{i\}\)，又强制 \(d(\{i\})=g(\{i\})−g(\varnothing )\)。继续增加集合，新的最高阶系数会被已经确定的低阶子集系数唯一决定；这解释了原论文按阶数归纳的直观路线。
proof_steps.justification: 函数外延性；论文适配使用固定有限总体。

lean_refs.explanation_md: funext S 在声明开头说明函数相等的含义。

shared_proofs.example_md:
取 \(N=\{1,2\}\)，并指定 \(g(\varnothing)=2\)、\(g(\{1\})=5\)、\(g(\{2\})=7\)、\(g(\{1,2\})=13\)。任何满足全部掩码重构的 d 都必须依次满足
\[d(\varnothing)=2,\quad d(\{1\})=5-2=3,\quad d(\{2\})=7-2=5,\]
\[d(\{1,2\})=13-2-3-5=3.\]
如果只要求完整输入输出等于 13，另一组 \(d(\varnothing),d(\{1\}),d(\{2\}),d(\{1,2\})=(0,0,0,13)\) 也能满足这一条等式，却在全掩码时输出 0、在单变量掩码时也输出 0。因此“所有 \(S\subseteq N\)”的量词不可删除。

theorem interaction_reconstruct (d : Game α) (S : Finset α) :
    interaction (reconstruct d) S = d S := by
  induction S using Finset.induction_on generalizing d with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert i S hi ih =>
    rw [interaction_insert _ _ _ hi]
    have h : interaction (marginal (reconstruct d) i) S =
        interaction (reconstruct (fun T => d (insert i T))) S := by
      apply interaction_congr
      intro T hT
      have hiT : i ∉ T := fun hit => hi (hT hit)
      simp only [marginal, reconstruct, sum_powerset_insert hiT, add_sub_cancel_left]
    rw [h, ih]

/-- Dividends are the unique coefficients that reconstruct all coalitions. -/

theorem reconstruction_unique (v d : Game α)
    (h : ∀ S, reconstruct d S = v S) : d = interaction v := by
  funext S
  rw [← interaction_reconstruct d S]
  apply interaction_congr
  intro T _
  exact h T

en.title: Shared proof: uniqueness of coefficients reconstructing all masks

assumptions.text_md: The coalition is finite. The games and coefficient functions are arbitrary real-valued functions on finite subsets; continuity, differentiability, independence and a zero output baseline are unnecessary.
The ambient universe may be infinite, but every coalition in a sum is finite. Paper applications fix a finite universe and use its powerset.
The same coefficients must reconstruct every finite subset in the domain, including the empty set. Reconstruction at one specified coalition is insufficient.

definitions.text_md: The interaction is a finite alternating sum. Since the summation subset is contained in the target, the cardinality difference in its exponent is a nonnegative integer.
Reconstruction sums all coefficients activated by the retained-variable set.
The insertion difference compares retaining the distinguished variable with masking it. The insertion lemma below is used only when that variable is absent from the target.

en.overview: Prove converse Möbius inversion for arbitrary coefficients, then substitute the reconstruction equality at every mask and conclude pointwise equality.
en.completion_scope: Coefficient uniqueness and the converse inversion actually used by the library; finite-universe paper quantifiers are recorded by separate adapters.
en.example_md: For two variables with mask outputs 2, 5, 7 and 13, the dividends are 2, 3, 5 and 3. Their full sum is 13, the empty-mask sum is 2, and singleton reconstruction gives 5 and 7. If only the full output 13 were required, coefficients 0, 0, 0 and 13 would also fit that one mask but fail all others. Hence the universal mask requirement matters.
caveats: Uniqueness concerns coefficients for one fixed game and the same AND activation rule. It does not assert uniqueness of every explanation framework, causal model or AND–OR decomposition.
The source inducts on cardinality; the library proves converse inversion. This text fully explains the route actually used by the library.
Every subset, including the empty one, must be reconstructed exactly. Fitting only the full input, or fitting approximately, does not satisfy the theorem.

proof_steps.title: Prove converse inversion at the empty set
proof_steps.body_md: First prove $I_{R_d}(S)=d(S)$ for an arbitrary coefficient function $d$, without using the reconstruction hypothesis. Induct on finite $S$ and keep $d$ universally quantified. At the empty set, $R_d(\varnothing)=d(\varnothing)$, and the empty interaction of this game has that same value. Thus the empty coefficient is fixed rather than an additional free parameter.
proof_steps.justification: The definitions and strengthened finite-set induction.

proof_steps.title: The difference of a reconstruction is another reconstruction
proof_steps.body_md: For $i\notin S$, define $e(U)=d(U\cup\{i\})$. Every $T\subseteq S$ excludes $i$, so splitting the subsets of $T\cup\{i\}$ gives $R_d(T\cup\{i\})=R_d(T)+\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U\cup\{i\})$. Subtraction leaves $R_e(T)$. This identity is used only for $T\subseteq S$: when $i\in T$, the two-family argument would no longer be disjoint.
proof_steps.justification: The subset partition, cancellation of finite sums, and the definition of the new coefficient function.

proof_steps.title: Use local equality to prove the insertion step
proof_steps.body_md: The insertion lemma gives $I_{R_d}(S\cup\{i\})=I_{\Delta_i R_d}(S)$. The interaction on $S$ reads only values at subsets of $S$, where the previous step proves that $\Delta_i R_d$ equals $R_e$. Hence its interaction equals $I_{R_e}(S)$. Apply the induction hypothesis for the arbitrary function $e$ to obtain $e(S)=d(S\cup\{i\})$. This proves converse inversion on the inserted set.
proof_steps.justification: Insertion differences, congruence on the subsets actually used, and strengthened induction.

proof_steps.title: Substitute the reconstruction hypothesis for every mask
proof_steps.body_md: Restore the assumption that the same $d$ satisfies $R_d(T)=g(T)$ at every finite $T$. For arbitrary $S$, converse inversion gives $d(S)=I_{R_d}(S)$. In this finite sum every argument $U$ is a subset of $S$, so the assumption replaces $R_d(U)$ by $g(U)$ term by term. The resulting sum is $I_g(S)$. Coefficients are not chosen afresh for each mask.
proof_steps.justification: Converse inversion and the reconstruction equality at each subset.

proof_steps.title: Conclude function equality and check the application domain
proof_steps.body_md: Since $S$ is arbitrary, equality at every finite input gives $d=I_g$. The public result quantifies over all finite subsets of a universe that may itself be infinite; a paper application restricts this universe to its finite $N$. In particular, the empty mask forces $d(\varnothing)=g(\varnothing)$, and a singleton forces $d(\{i\})=g(\{i\})-g(\varnothing)$. Higher coefficients are then fixed by the already determined proper-subset coefficients.
proof_steps.justification: Function extensionality and the finite-universe paper specialization.

en.title: Shared proof: symmetry of interactions
assumptions: $S\subseteq N$, $i,j\in N\setminus S$; for every $U\subseteq S$, $g(U\cup\{i\})=g(U\cup\{j\})$.

proof_steps.body_md: Since $i,j\notin S$, every subset of $S\cup\{i\}$ uniquely has the form $U$ or $U\cup\{i\}$ for $U\subseteq S$. Insertion increases cardinality by one, giving opposite signs. en.title: Shared auxiliary proof: finite factorial convolution, including empty boundaries
assumptions: $T,E\subseteq N$, $T\cap E=\varnothing$; $k\in\mathbb N$, $k>0$; $m=|E|$.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Write $w_A=I_g(A)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, and $w_\varnothing=b$. The finite difference is $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}g(L\cup S)$. No zero output baseline is assumed. Centering $g_0=g-b$ removes only the empty dividend.

proof_steps.title: Prove the finite factorial convolution
proof_steps.body_md: For finite $R$ of size $m$, define $F_R(a,b)=\sum_{A\subseteq R}(a+|A|)!(b+m-|A|)!$. Induct on $R$ with the statement strengthened to every nonnegative $a,b$. At the empty set both sides are $a!b!$. Inserting a new element splits the sum as $F_R(a,b+1)+F_R(a+1,b)$. The induction expressions share denominator $(a+b+2)!$ and large factorial $(a+b+m+2)!$. The smaller factorials combine as $a!(b+1)!+(a+1)!b!=a!b!(a+b+2)$. Cancelling this positive factor proves the formula on the inserted set. Every factorial denominator is positive; zero values of $a,b,m$ are included.

proof_steps.title: Sum weights over all supersets of a fixed subset
proof_steps.body_md: Let $k>0$, $L\subseteq E$, $m=|E|$, $l=|L|$ and $R=E\setminus L$. Each $S$ with $L\subseteq S\subseteq E$ uniquely equals $L\cup A$ with $A\subseteq R$. Thus $|S|=l+|A|$ and $|R|=m-l$. Apply the preceding convolution with $a=l$ and $b=k-1$. Use $k(k-1)!=k!$ and cancel the positive large factorial $(m+k)!$ to obtain the displayed weight sum. Both $L=\varnothing$ and $L=E$ are included.

proof_steps.title: Exchange the sums to obtain the weighted finite-difference transform
proof_steps.body_md: Disjointness of $T,E$ gives $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq S}w_{T\cup U}$. Every pair $U\subseteq S\subseteq E$ occurs exactly once, so exchange the finite sums. For fixed $U$, the preceding superset-weight identity supplies precisely the displayed coefficient of $w_{T\cup U}$.

en.title: Shared proof: all three branches of the Shapley–Taylor index
assumptions: $T\subseteq N$; the original three-branch STI definition at a positive integer order $k>0$. The source does not explicitly state $k>0$; this is the positive-order domain interpretation. Order zero is outside the present verification scope.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Write $w_A=I_g(A)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, and $w_\varnothing=b$. The finite difference is $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}g(L\cup S)$. No zero output baseline is assumed. Centering $g_0=g-b$ removes only the empty dividend.

proof_steps.title: Handle the lower and higher order branches
proof_steps.body_md: At a positive order $k$, if $|T|<k$, the finite difference in the empty environment is $w_T$ by definition; for an empty target its value is $b$. If $|T|>k$, the definition gives zero. These branches require neither division by $n$ nor $n\ge k$.

proof_steps.title: Convert the top-order weight to the shared factorial weight
proof_steps.body_md: If $|T|=k$, positivity and $T\subseteq N$ give $n\ge k\ge1$, so division by $n$ is valid. Put $E=N\setminus T$ and $m=n-k$. For $S\subseteq E$, its size $s$ satisfies $s\le m\le n-1$, making the relevant binomial coefficient positive. Expand its factorial definition and use $k(k-1)!=k!$ to obtain the displayed shared weight.

proof_steps.title: Prove the finite factorial convolution
Sum weights over all supersets of a fixed subset
Exchange the sums to obtain the weighted finite-difference transform
Apply the shared identity at the top order
proof_steps.body_md: The target and environment are disjoint and $k>0$, so the weighted finite-difference identity yields coefficient $\binom{|U|+k}{k}^{-1}$. Combining this with the lower and higher order definition branches proves the full three-branch statement.

proof_steps.title: Check empty targets and two positive orders
proof_steps.body_md: For the outputs 7, 8, 9 and 13, the dividends are 7, 1, 2 and 3. At $k=1$, the empty target has value 7, the singletons have values $5/2$ and $7/2$, and the pair is above the order and has value zero. At $k=2$, the four values are 7, 1, 2 and 3, summing to 13. If the universe is empty and $k\ge1$, only the lower-order empty target remains with value $b$. Positive order is the stated scope interpretation; the source does not explicitly print the inequality.

assumptions: $i\in N\setminus S$; $S\ne\varnothing$; $c\in\mathbb R$; for every $U\subseteq S$, $g(U\cup\{i\})=g(U)+c$.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. proof_steps.title: State the exact domain of the valid public property
proof_steps.body_md: This public result requires $S\ne\varnothing$ and has different quantifiers from the false CVPR proposition; it cannot replace that proposition. Since $i\notin S$ and the marginal is the constant $c$, the interaction containing $i$ equals the interaction of the constant game $c$ on $S$.
proof_steps.justification: The original Sparse statement can use this result if it already excludes empty environments; the original CVPR statement cannot.

proof_steps.title: Cancel all subsets by an explicit pairing
proof_steps.body_md: Pair subsets with and without $i$ to obtain $I_g(S\cup\{i\})=c\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}$. proof_steps.justification: No assumption $g(\varnothing)=0$ is needed; the premises imply $c=g(\{i\})-g(\varnothing)$.

shared_proofs.title: 共享完整证明：真实混合偏导零与矩形有限差分
shared_proofs.statement_tex: \left[\forall z\in\mathbb R^n,\ \forall\kappa\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\kappa|\ge M+1:\ D^\kappa v(z)\text{存在且为}0\right]\ \Longrightarrow\ \forall S\subseteq N,\ |S|\ge M+1:\ I(S)=0

definitions.body_md: 固定 $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$、模型 $v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$、输入 $x$ 与输入基线 $r$。掩码在集合 $A$ 内取 $x_i$，其余取 $r_i$，定义 $g(A)=v(x_A)$、$b=g(\varnothing)$、$g_0(A)=g(A)-b$。原Sparse交互为 $I(A)=I_{g_0}(A)=\sum_{L\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|L|}g_0(L)$，故 $I(\varnothing)=0$。$e_i$ 是坐标单位向量；$a_i=x_i-r_i$ 是第 $i$ 个坐标的实际掩码增量。

proof_steps.title: 把原混合导数的存在与顺序展开
proof_steps.body_md: 经典偏导定义为 $D_i f(z)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}f(z+t e_i)\right|_{t=0}$。这等于把其余坐标固定、以第 $i$ 个坐标值为参数的普通导数。用非降序坐标列表 $(i_1,\ldots,i_q)$ 编码多重指标 $\kappa_i$：它等于列表中 $i$ 的出现次数，$q=\sum_i\kappa_i$。从左到右依次取偏导，定义 $P_0=v$、$P_j=D_{i_j}P_{j-1}$。原1-β的经典“混合导数存在且为零”要求相应前缀偏导沿下一坐标的导数真实存在，并给出 $P_q(z)=0$ 对全部 $z$。项目把这些存在条件与高阶零值一起编码在同一个1-β谓词中，只对原要求的 $q>M$ 列表使用它；没有另加所有低阶导数全局光滑的假设。原C1背景保留，但C1本身不保证高阶导数存在。原分母排写未另说明操作顺序，项目固定升序依次取导；如果采用反序约定，通用差分引理按同样的反序使用即可，不靠混合偏导换序。

proof_steps.body_md: 定义有限差分 $\delta_{a,i}f(z)=f(z+a e_i)-f(z)$。如果 $f$ 沿坐标 $i$ 在每个点可微，则任何有限个平移后的加减也沿该坐标可微。平移不改变曲线导数：$D_i(f(\cdot+h))(z)=D_i f(z+h)$，因为 $(z+t e_i)+h=(z+h)+t e_i$。再由普通一元导数的差法则，得 $D_i(\delta_{a,j}f)=\delta_{a,j}(D_i f)$。对差分个数归纳，任意有限矩形差分都与这个真实偏导交换；这里只使用平移和有限加减，不使用高阶方向链式公式或无限级数。

proof_steps.body_md: 对坐标列表长度 $q$ 归纳，并允许任意方向和任意实数步长。空列表时，矩形差分与零阶偏导都是 $f$；假设它恒零即得结论。对非空列表，先取第一个方向 $i_1$，其余差分记为 $R$。原前缀存在条件说明 $D_{i_1}f$ 沿剩余取导顺序可微，而其最终混合导数恒零。归纳假设给 $R(D_{i_1}f)=0$。上一辅助引理于是给 $D_{i_1}(Rf)=R(D_{i_1}f)=0$。对每个固定 $z$，一元函数 $H(t)=(Rf)(z+t e_{i_1})$ 在全实线上可微，且 $H\prime(t)=0$。一元均值定理推出 $H(a_{i_1})=H(0)$，即 $\delta_{a_{i_1},i_1}Rf(z)=0$。负步长、零步长都在全实线结论内，不需另加输入区间或正增量条件。

en.title: Complete shared proof: zero classical mixed partials and rectangular differences
en.overview: Globally zero classical mixed partials give zero rectangular differences. The actual coordinate-mask alternating sum is that difference; nonempty centering then recovers the original interaction.
assumptions: The original C1-function setting is retained. Global high-order mixed partials in 1-β are interpreted as classical existing derivatives; required prefix differentiability unfolds their definition and is not replaced by a total Lean deriv function returning zero.
All masks use the same fixed input baseline r and M∈ℕ. No analyticity, infinite Taylor representation, or polynomial premise is added.

definitions.body_md: Fix $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, x, and r. The coordinate mask keeps x_i on A and r_i elsewhere. Let $g(A)=v(x_A)$, $b=g(\varnothing)$, and $g_0(A)=g(A)-b$. The source interaction is $I(A)=I_{g_0}(A)$, with empty value zero. Let e_i be the coordinate unit vector and $a_i=x_i-r_i$ the actual masking increment.

proof_steps.title: Classical mixed partials and their existence order
proof_steps.body_md: The classical partial is $D_i f(z)=\left.\frac d{dt}f(z+t e_i)\right|_{t=0}$. Encode a multiindex by a nondecreasing coordinate list $(i_1,\ldots,i_q)$, and define $P_0=v$, $P_j=D_{i_j}P_{j-1}$. Classical existence of the stated mixed partials includes actual differentiability of each required prefix along the next coordinate, and 1-β gives $P_q\equiv0$. These existence conditions and the zero value are encoded together; only lists q>M are used. No extra global smoothness of all low derivatives is assumed. C1 alone does not imply existence of high derivatives. A fixed ascending order is used; a reverse convention can use the same difference argument in reverse order, without interchanging mixed partials.

proof_steps.body_md: Define $\delta_{a,i}f(z)=f(z+a e_i)-f(z)$. If f is differentiable along coordinate i everywhere, its finitely many translated sums and differences are too. Translation gives $D_i(f(\cdot+h))(z)=D_i f(z+h)$ because $(z+t e_i)+h=(z+h)+t e_i$. The one-variable difference rule yields $D_i(\delta_{a,j}f)=\delta_{a,j}(D_i f)$. Induction extends this to arbitrary finite rectangular differences. Only translations and finite additions are used, with no infinite series or higher directional chain rule.

For the empty list, both the difference and the order-zero partial are f, and its assumed zero value proves the claim. For a nonempty list, let R denote the remaining differences. en.title: Shared proof: exact reconstruction by the OR complement transform
assumptions: $T\subseteq N$; $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$. Nonempty OR dividends are the negative AND transform of the complement game; the empty OR dividend is the original output baseline.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Write $w_A=I_g(A)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, and $w_\varnothing=b$. The finite difference is $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}g(L\cup S)$. No zero output baseline is assumed. Centering $g_0=g-b$ removes only the empty dividend. For nonempty targets, $O_g^N(S)=-I_{g^c}(S)$ where $g^c(L)=g(N\setminus L)$; the empty OR coefficient is $g(\varnothing)$.

proof_steps.title: Intersecting subsets are a difference of two powersets
proof_steps.body_md: For $T\subseteq N$ and $S\subseteq N$, disjointness from $T$ is equivalent to $S\subseteq N\setminus T$. Therefore the intersecting family is $\mathcal P(N)\setminus\mathcal P(N\setminus T)$. The second powerset is contained in the first, so its sum is subtracted from the full sum. The empty set belongs to both full families and to neither intersecting family.

proof_steps.title: Reconstruct the negative complement game twice
proof_steps.body_md: Let $f(L)=-h(N\setminus L)$. Linearity shows that each nonempty OR coefficient equals $I_f(S)$. Every intersecting set is nonempty, so substitute these coefficients throughout the intersecting sum. Apply reconstruction on $N$ and on $N\setminus T$ to obtain $f(N)-f(N\setminus T)=-h(\varnothing)+h(T)$. The final complement equality uses the checked premise $T\subseteq N$.

proof_steps.title: Add back the separately defined empty OR baseline
proof_steps.body_md: The empty OR coefficient is $h(\varnothing)=v_{or}(x_\varnothing)$. Adding it to the intersecting sum gives $v_{or}(x_T)$. For empty $T$, the intersecting family is empty and only the baseline remains; for $T=N$, the full output is recovered. This also avoids double-counting source cases when $T$ is empty.

definitions.body_md: 本条改用分布平均熵游戏$H_Y(S)=H(Y\mid X_S)=E[-\sum_y p(y\mid X_S)\log p(y\mid X_S)]$。此条件期望对输入分布积分，不要求输入空间有限；原离散数据情形等于$\sum_{x_S}p(x_S)[-\sum_y p(y\mid x_S)\log p(y\mid x_S)]$。它不是某个固定x的单次模型输出g_x。零质量项按0log0=0，条件熵须有限。条件MI定义为$H_Y(S)-H_Y(Si)$，co-information定义为该量减去$H_Y(Sj)-H_Y(Sij)$，采用原Eq7约定。

en.title: Co-information identity of four conditional entropies
assumptions: The four conditional entropies are finite and use the source Equation (7) co-information sign; X need not be a finite type.

definitions.body_md: This entry uses the population entropy game $H_Y(S)=H(Y\mid X_S)=E[-\sum_y p(y\mid X_S)\log p(y\mid X_S)]$. This conditional expectation integrates over the input law and does not require a finite input space; the source discrete-data case is $\sum_{x_S}p(x_S)[-\sum_y p(y\mid x_S)\log p(y\mid x_S)]$. It is distinct from a single fixed-input output g_x. Zero-mass terms use 0log0=0, and the conditional entropies must be finite. Conditional MI is $H_Y(S)-H_Y(Si)$, and co-information subtracts $H_Y(Sj)-H_Y(Sij)$, as in the source Equation (7).

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：有限多项式支持与二值掩码
assumptions: 有限坐标总体；有限单项式索引集P，每项k的支持A_k与自然次数d_{k,i}满足i∈A_k时严格正；每项实系数c_k，不要求支持互异。

definitions.body_md: $P$ 为有限项索引集，$A_k,d_{k,i},c_k$ 为各项支持、次数、系数；$K_A=\sum_{k\in P:A_k=A}c_km_{A_k}(z)$。$z_i=x_i-r_i$ 为增量，$z_i^S=z_i$（i∈S）、0（其余）；$m_A(z)=\prod_{i\in A}z_i^{d_i}$。

shared_proofs.overview: 定义单项式 $m_A(z)=\prod_{i\in A}z_i^{d_i}$，其中每个 $d_i>0$；掩码增量坐标为 $z_i\mathbf1_{i\in S}$。若 $A\subseteq S$，每个因子不变；若不是，取 $i\in A\setminus S$，正次零因子使全积零。这给精确支持律。
shared_proofs.proof_scope: 实际Lean证明单项式遮罩律、任意有限项索引多项式的遮罩和、按支持分组重构及真实Möbius交互等于支持贡献；同支持不同次数可同时存在。另验证非零参考贡献的二值归一化。无限Taylor收敛与任意DNN不是本共享命题。

proof_steps.title: 检查正次单项式的遮罩
proof_steps.body_md: 定义单项式 $m_A(z)=\prod_{i\in A}z_i^{d_i}$，其中每个 $d_i>0$；掩码增量坐标为 $z_i\mathbf1_{i\in S}$。若 $A\subseteq S$，每个因子不变；若不是，取 $i\in A\setminus S$，正次零因子使全积零。这给精确支持律。

proof_steps.title: 分组支持并归一化非零贡献
proof_steps.body_md: 对有限个单项式逐项应用支持律，将同支持的贡献累加为 $K_A$。全部掩码输出为 $\sum_{A\subseteq S}K_A$，有限 Möbius 唯一性给 $K_A=I_g(A)$，包括空支持常数。若 $u=K_A(x)\ne0$，则 $K_A(x_S)/u=\mathbf1_{A\subseteq S}$。不声称无限 Taylor 在任意网络收敛。

en.title: Shared proof: finite-polynomial support and binary masks
en.overview: Define $m_A(z)=\prod_{i\in A}z_i^{d_i}$ with every $d_i>0$ and masked increment coordinates $z_i\mathbf1_{i\in S}$. If $A\subseteq S$, every factor is retained. Otherwise choose $i\in A\setminus S$; its positive-degree zero factor annihilates the product. This proves the exact support identity.
assumptions: A finite coordinate universe and finite monomial index set P. Each support A_k has strictly positive natural degrees on its coordinates and a real coefficient c_k. Distinct terms may share a support.

definitions.body_md: Let P index finitely many terms, with support A_k, degrees d_{k,i} and coefficients c_k. Put $K_A=\sum_{k\in P:A_k=A}c_km_{A_k}(z)$. The increment is $z_i=x_i-r_i$, with $z_i^S=z_i$ in S and zero elsewhere. Define $m_A(z)=\prod_{i\in A}z_i^{d_i}$.

en.proof_scope: Lean proves monomial masking, masked sums for arbitrary finite term indices, reconstruction grouped by support, and equality of actual Möbius dividends to support contributions. Equal supports with different degrees are allowed. Nonzero reference normalization is also verified. Infinite Taylor convergence and arbitrary DNNs are outside this shared claim.

proof_steps.title: Mask positive-degree monomials
proof_steps.body_md: Define $m_A(z)=\prod_{i\in A}z_i^{d_i}$ with every $d_i>0$ and masked increment coordinates $z_i\mathbf1_{i\in S}$. If $A\subseteq S$, every factor is retained. Otherwise choose $i\in A\setminus S$; its positive-degree zero factor annihilates the product. This proves the exact support identity.

proof_steps.title: Group supports and normalize nonzero contributions
proof_steps.body_md: Apply this identity to every term in a finite polynomial and group equal supports into $K_A$. All mask outputs equal $\sum_{A\subseteq S}K_A$, so finite Möbius uniqueness identifies $K_A=I_g(A)$, including the constant empty support. If $u=K_A(x)\ne0$, normalization gives $K_A(x_S)/u=\mathbf1_{A\subseteq S}$. No convergence of an infinite Taylor series for an arbitrary network is claimed.

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：独立随机量的乘积矩与平方残差
assumptions: 概率测度、可测独立的有限随机量族；每个因子具有有限二阶矩。残差子结论另取中心化噪声和指定方差。

definitions.body_md: $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$、$\epsilon_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$；$E$是真实概率积分，$\operatorname{Var}X=E(X-EX)^2$。$r,w_i$ 为固定实数，$q_i$为噪声方差；Gaussian子结论通过map-law规定分布。

shared_proofs.overview: 在概率测度下，独立可测随机量 $X_i$ 各有有限二阶矩，独立乘积可积且有有限二阶矩。对 $X_i$ 及 $X_i^2$ 分别使用乘积积分分解，得 $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$，$E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$。用 $EX_i^2=(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i$，相减得乘积方差 $\prod_i[(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i]-\prod_i(EX_i)^2$。
shared_proofs.proof_scope: 实际积分产品矩、乘积L2、中心化残差期望与Gaussian矩前提的推导全部编译；本篇具体适配与其他论文的缩放分别提供。

proof_steps.title: 分解独立产品的一阶与二阶积分
proof_steps.body_md: 在概率测度下，独立可测随机量 $X_i$ 各有有限二阶矩，独立乘积可积且有有限二阶矩。对 $X_i$ 及 $X_i^2$ 分别使用乘积积分分解，得 $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$，$E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$。用 $EX_i^2=(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i$，相减得乘积方差 $\prod_i[(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i]-\prod_i(EX_i)^2$。

proof_steps.title: 计算中心化加权残差
proof_steps.body_md: 若 $\epsilon_i$ 独立、中心化、方差为$q_i$，有限加权和 $Z=\sum_iw_i\epsilon_i$ 均值零、方差 $\sum_iw_i^2q_i$，故 $E(r+Z)^2=r^2+\sum_iw_i^2q_i$。这是真实积分，不是形式矩占位。

proof_steps.title: 由 Gaussian 映射律得到矩
proof_steps.body_md: Gaussian法则进一步提供所有矩前提：从映射分布 $\mu\circ\epsilon_i^{-1}=\mathcal N(0,q_i)$ 推出 L2、均值0和方差$q_i$；平移因子 $1+\epsilon_i$ 独立、均值1、方差$q$，于是积均值1、方差$(1+q)^s-1$。本篇用于Lemma1的独立子模型和Theorem3逐行噪声残差；BNN/Difficulty将另显式适配坐标缩放与参考系数。

en.title: Shared proof: independent-product moments and squared residuals
en.overview: Under a probability measure, measurable independent $X_i$ with finite second moments have an integrable product with finite second moment. Factor the integrals for $X_i$ and $X_i^2$: $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$ and $E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$. Substitute $EX_i^2=(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i$ and subtract the mean square to obtain the product-variance formula $\prod_i[(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i]-\prod_i(EX_i)^2$.
assumptions: A probability measure and a finite measurable independent family with finite second moments. The residual subresult additionally uses centered noises with specified variances.

definitions.body_md: $X_i,\epsilon_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$; E denotes an actual probability integral and variance is $E(X-EX)^2$. Residual r and weights w_i are fixed reals, while q_i are noise variances; the Gaussian subresult specifies laws through map-laws.

proof_steps.title: Compute centered weighted residuals
proof_steps.body_md: For independent centered $\epsilon_i$ with variances $q_i$, the finite weighted sum $Z=\sum_iw_i\epsilon_i$ has mean zero and variance $\sum_iw_i^2q_i$. Therefore $E(r+Z)^2=r^2+\sum_iw_i^2q_i$. These are actual integrals, rather than formal moment placeholders.

assumptions.body_md: Gate variables of the network are finite and discrete. All conditional and joint laws belong to the same distribution; prefixes and suffixes use the same samples, without requiring every gate pattern to occur.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

For a binary gate vector, let $p_d$ be its marginals and define $TC(p)=D_{KL}(p\Vert\prod_dp_d)$ and $C=\sum_dH(p_d)$. Define $TC(\Sigma\mid Y)=\sum_yp_yTC(p(\Sigma\mid y))$ and $C_{\mid Y}=\sum_yp_y\sum_dH(p(\Sigma^d\mid y))$. A positive joint atom has positive corresponding marginal atoms, so KL is defined on the actual support.

en.overview: For every positive joint gate atom, split $\log[p(\sigma)/\prod_dp_d(\sigma_d)]$. Zero atoms contribute zero. The joint entropy cancels the $\log p(\sigma)$ term in KL, leaving a sum of marginal log terms.

proof_steps.title: Expand the actual KL definition
proof_steps.body_md: For every positive joint gate atom, split $\log[p(\sigma)/\prod_dp_d(\sigma_d)]$. Zero atoms contribute zero. The joint entropy cancels the $\log p(\sigma)$ term in KL, leaving a sum of marginal log terms.

proof_steps.title: Sum by marginal projection
proof_steps.body_md: Interchange the finite sums and push forward along $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_d$. Each term becomes $-\sum_b p_d(b)\log p_d(b)=H(p_d)$. Therefore $H(\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)=\sum_dH(\Sigma_l^d)=C_l$, exactly for every finite-dimensional binary gate law.

Interchange the finite sums and push forward along $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_d$. Each term becomes $-\sum_b p_d(b)\log p_d(b)=H(p_d)$. Therefore $H(\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)=\sum_dH(\Sigma_l^d)=C_l$, exactly for every finite-dimensional binary gate law.

en.title: Fréchet gradient of true finite-EBM likelihood

assumptions.body_md: During the EBM update, DNN gate data and the prior q are frozen. Parameters may lie in any real normed space; every finite-state score is Fréchet differentiable. The empirical law r is normalized. If q is its actual marginal product, no extra positive-rate assumption is needed.

definitions.body_md: The gate state space $\mathcal S$ is finite, the prior $q$ is normalized and the score $f_\theta$ is real. Define $Z_\theta=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}$ and $p_\theta(s)=q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}/Z_\theta$. The prior is positive on the true empirical support of $r$; this follows for the actual product of gate marginals, including activation rates zero or one.

en.overview: A positive empirical joint atom has positive corresponding marginals, so their product q is positive on the support of r. Apply the log-probability identity there, with zero empirical atoms contributing zero, to obtain the true $-E_r\log p_\theta=\log Z-E_r(f+\log q)$. Activation rates zero and one remain allowed.

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：真实 dropout 与最大池化的固定门仿射作用

assumptions.body_md: 固定keep位；每个池化窗口非空有限。门区域中固定选择仍达到实际预激活的最大值；并列时只选一个。

definitions.body_md: $D_k(h)_d=k_dh_d$，$M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$，$a(p)\in R_p$ 为一个达到最大值的输入，$P_a(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$；输入窗口与输出索引域可以不同。

shared_proofs.overview: 原 Appendix A 的保留位 $k_d\in\{0,1\}$ 给真实输出 $D_k(h)_d=k_dh_d$。Boolean keep 的 public dropoutLinear 正是保留坐标或置零；分别检查保留/删除两支，得到加法与标量乘法保持。故 $D_k(Wx+b)=(D_k\circ W)x+D_k(b)$，偏置同样被门作用，不被丢掉。这里固定的是实际采样所得 keep 位，不假定带随机门的整个网络全局仿射。

proof_steps.title: Construct one maximizing selector from actual max pooling
proof_steps.body_md: Each output window $R_p$ is a nonempty finite set of input indices, with actual pool value $M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$. A finite maximum is attained; public maximizingSelector chooses one attaining input per window, including ties. Thus $M(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$, without adding tied maxima. A fixed gate region requires the same $a(p)\in R_p$ to maximize the actual preactivation. Proving that the finite supremum equals its selected value yields $M(Wx+b)=(P_a\circ W)x+P_a(b)$. These actual linear actions are absorbed into the preceding affine chain weights and biases; layer_comp retains the final bias. The source pooling input-index slip remains separately recorded.

shared_proofs.statement_tex: Z_i\sim N(1,q_i),\quad EJ_T=\prod_{i\in T}m_i,\quad VarJ_T=\prod_{i\in T}(m_i^2+d_i)-\prod_{i\in T}m_i^2,\quad E Z_i^{k_i}\ge1
assumptions: 有限独立Gaussian坐标及自然次数；所有矩/L2从法则得到。正方差/增长子结论另用q_i>0、k_i>0及非空不交旧/新增支持。

definitions.body_md: $J_T=\prod_{i\in T}|Z_i|^{k_i}$、$m_i=E|Z_i|^{k_i}$、$d_i=Var|Z_i|^{k_i}$。E与Var为概率积分；$Z_i=1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau$是原坐标Gaussian的可测仿射变换。最低交互另为$U_{ref}\prod Z_i$。

shared_proofs.overview: Gaussian随机量Y的map-law给任意有限p的Lp。对正整数k选p=2k，用范数实幂变换得 $|Y|^k\in L^2$；k=0为常数1。坐标可测变换保留独立，实际乘积也L2，Fubini产品积分给其均值/方差公式。这使用已发布dyn-shared-independent-residual的真实产品证明，不重复建立形式矩代数库。

proof_steps.title: 从Gaussian法则取得所有幂的L2
proof_steps.body_md: Gaussian随机量Y的map-law给任意有限p的Lp。对正整数k选p=2k，用范数实幂变换得 $|Y|^k\in L^2$；k=0为常数1。坐标可测变换保留独立，实际乘积也L2，Fubini产品积分给其均值/方差公式。这使用已发布dyn-shared-independent-residual的真实产品证明，不重复建立形式矩代数库。

proof_steps.title: 由反射与无原子证明实际量化条件
proof_steps.body_md: 对 $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$，反射 $Z\mapsto2-Z$ 同律。二项式展开中 $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$：令 $t=z-1$，奇次项相消、偶次项非负，常数项为2。积分得 $EZ^k\ge1$；逐点 $|z|^k\ge z^k$ 给 $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$。任意 Gaussian 整数幂均 L2。若 $q>0,k>0$ 且绝对幂方差为零，则它几乎处处为常数；其每个水平集最多两个点，与 Gaussian 无原子矛盾，故方差严格正。独立乘积公式继而给非空积的正方差。

proof_steps.title: 分解不交支持并比较实际增长比
proof_steps.body_md:
记 $a=EA$、$b_B=EB$、$v_A=\operatorname{Var}A$、$v_B=\operatorname{Var}B$。支持不交且坐标独立给 $EAB=ab_B$ 与 $\operatorname{Var}(AB)=v_A(b_B^2+v_B)+a^2v_B$。在上述域 $a\ge1,b_B\ge1,v_A>0,v_B>0$，所以 $\operatorname{Var}(AB)/v_A>b_B^2$。令 $p=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}EZ_i^{\pi_i\prime}$，有 $b_B\ge p\ge1$，从而原方差下界成立。原 Theorem2.3 的错误精确矩替换不再作为推理前提。

由于期望均正，$K_{S\prime}/K_S=b_Bv_A/\operatorname{Var}(AB)<1/b_B\le1/p\le1$。实际 Lean 用整个旧/新增坐标 Gaussian 家族的积分证明两项不等式，所有正方差与矩下界均已由分布律消去，不假设待证结论。$S=\varnothing$ 时 $J_S=1$，$\sigma=0$ 时全部触发恒1；原比值均含0分母。源文未给该边界的实数约定，因此不将 Lean 的总除法零值作为作者约定。

proof_steps.title: 适配有符号最低交互与原绝对触发
proof_steps.body_md: 最低交互用固定参考幅值乘 $\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$，无需截尾，其均值/方差为 $U_{ref}$ 与 $U_{ref}^2[(1+q)^s-1]$。另一方面原绝对触发逐坐标严格满足 $|s_i\tau+\epsilon_i|/\tau=|1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau|$（$s_i^2=1,\tau>0$）。仿射map-law给均值1的Gaussian因子，加入σ正条件后实际产品增长定理直接适用。F08 PaperBayesian显式适配；F10后续复用同一共享库，但保留其原J矩错误。

en.overview: A Gaussian map-law gives Lp for every finite p. For positive integer k, choose p=2k and apply the norm power transform to obtain $|Y|^k\in L^2$; k=0 gives constant one. Measurable coordinate transforms preserve independence, the actual product is L2, and Fubini factorization gives its moments. This reuses the published actual-product proof dyn-shared-independent-residual rather than duplicating a formal moment-algebra library.
assumptions: Finite independent Gaussian coordinates and natural degrees, with all moments/L2 derived from laws. Positive variance and growth additionally use q_i>0,k_i>0 and nonempty disjoint old/added supports.

definitions.body_md: $J_T=\prod_{i\in T}|Z_i|^{k_i}$, $m_i=E|Z_i|^{k_i}$ and $d_i=Var|Z_i|^{k_i}$. E and Var are probability integrals. The source coordinates give measurable affine factors $Z_i=1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau$. The lowest dividend separately equals $U_{ref}\prod Z_i$.

proof_steps.title: Obtain L2 of every power from Gaussian laws
proof_steps.body_md: A Gaussian map-law gives Lp for every finite p. For positive integer k, choose p=2k and apply the norm power transform to obtain $|Y|^k\in L^2$; k=0 gives constant one. Measurable coordinate transforms preserve independence, the actual product is L2, and Fubini factorization gives its moments. This reuses the published actual-product proof dyn-shared-independent-residual rather than duplicating a formal moment-algebra library.

proof_steps.title: Prove quantitative conditions using reflection and non-atomicity
proof_steps.body_md: For $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$, reflection $Z\mapsto2-Z$ preserves the law. The binomial expansion gives $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$: with $t=z-1$, odd terms cancel, even terms are nonnegative and the constant term is two. Integration yields $EZ^k\ge1$. Pointwise $|z|^k\ge z^k$ gives $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$. Every Gaussian integer power is L2. If $q>0,k>0$ and the absolute power had zero variance, it would be almost surely constant. Each level set contains at most two points, contradicting the absence of Gaussian atoms. Its variance is therefore positive; the independent-product formula gives positive variance for every nonempty product.

proof_steps.title: Split disjoint supports and compare actual growth ratios
proof_steps.body_md:
Write $a=EA$, $b_B=EB$, $v_A=\operatorname{Var}A$ and $v_B=\operatorname{Var}B$. Disjoint supports and independent coordinates give $EAB=ab_B$ and $\operatorname{Var}(AB)=v_A(b_B^2+v_B)+a^2v_B$. On the stated domain, $a\ge1,b_B\ge1,v_A>0,v_B>0$, so $\operatorname{Var}(AB)/v_A>b_B^2$. For $p=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}EZ_i^{\pi_i\prime}$, we have $b_B\ge p\ge1$, proving the source variance lower bound. The incorrect exact moment replacement in Theorem 2.3 is not used as a premise.

All means are positive, so $K_{S\prime}/K_S=b_Bv_A/\operatorname{Var}(AB)<1/b_B\le1/p\le1$. Actual Lean integrals of the complete old/added Gaussian coordinate family prove both inequalities, with positive variances and moment lower bounds discharged from distribution laws. If $S=\varnothing$, then $J_S=1$; if $\sigma=0$, all triggers equal one. Both cases give zero denominators. The source supplies no ordinary-real convention there, and Lean’s total division is not treated as an author convention.

proof_steps.title: Adapt the signed lowest dividend and original absolute trigger
proof_steps.body_md: The lowest dividend is a fixed reference amplitude times $\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$, giving exact untruncated mean $U_{ref}$ and variance $U_{ref}^2[(1+q)^s-1]$. The original absolute trigger instead satisfies $|s_i\tau+\epsilon_i|/\tau=|1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau|$ when $s_i^2=1,\tau>0$. The affine map-law gives mean-one Gaussian factors, and positive noise makes the actual-product growth theorem applicable. PaperBayesian explicitly adapts F08; F10 reuses the same library while retaining its original J-moment errors.

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：独立特征损失的唯一全局最优
assumptions: 固定有限两两独立L2随机特征，均值ai、严格正方差di；Gaussian实例从map-law消去矩前提。

definitions.body_md: 有限索引 $i$ 对应作者概念 $S$，$C_i$ 是固定的随机特征函数，$w_i$ 对应作者优化变量 $U_S$，$y^*$ 是固定标签。$a,d,w\in\mathbb R^k$；矩阵 $K=\operatorname{diag}d+aa^\top$。$L(w)=E(y^*-\sum_iw_iC_i)^2$ 是原期望平方损失。

shared_proofs.overview: 中心化 $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$，两两独立性与有限 L2 给 $E\eta_i=0$ 和交叉协方差0。于是 $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$。这是原随机特征的积分恒等式，不预设正规方程。
shared_proofs.proof_scope: 实际积分损失展开、对角加外积正定、显式正规方程及完成平方唯一全局最优均已证明。仅作为明确模型内的公共结论，不解决原零方差域或BNN替代近似。

proof_steps.title: 将真实损失展开为均值误差与方差罚项
proof_steps.body_md: 中心化 $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$，两两独立性与有限 L2 给 $E\eta_i=0$ 和交叉协方差0。于是 $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$。这是原随机特征的积分恒等式，不预设正规方程。

proof_steps.title: 验证显式候选与正定性
proof_steps.body_md: $d_i>0$ 时对任意非零 $h$，$h^\top Kh=\sum_id_ih_i^2+(a^\top h)^2>0$。设 $t=\sum_i a_i^2/d_i\ge0$、$\lambda=y^*/(1+t)$，令 $w_i^*=\lambda a_i/d_i$。直接计算 $a^\top w^*=\lambda t$，故 $(Kw^*)_i=d_iw_i^*+a_i(a^\top w^*)=a_i\lambda(1+t)=y^*a_i$。无需 Cramer 行列式的省略步骤。

proof_steps.title: 完成平方并消去Gaussian实例的矩条件
proof_steps.body_md: $Kw^*=y^*a$ 与正定K给 $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$ 对每个不同w成立。因此是真正唯一全局最优。在额外给定 $C_i\sim N(a_i,d_i)$ 的独立Gaussian实例中，map-law直接证明L2、均值ai、方差di，代入同一积分损失定理；不是将这些矩作为希望成立的假设。F08用固定概念触发，F10用Gaussian概念特征；不同原命题的错误或域限制各自在paper adapter保留。

proof_steps.title: First prove exact support of masked dividends
proof_steps.body_md: If $S\subseteq T$, every $L\subseteq S$ used in the dividend satisfies $L\cap T=L$, so the dividend is unchanged. Otherwise choose $i\in S\setminus T$. Inserting $i$ changes no output of the further-masked game, and finite-difference dummy cancellation gives $I_{g_T}(S)=0$. Thus $I_{g_T}(S)=\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}I_g(S)$, preserving any nonzero output baseline.

proof_steps.title: Nonzero normalization equals the AND criterion
proof_steps.body_md: Divide the actual support identity by nonzero I_g(S) to get $I_{g_T}(S)/I_g(S)=\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}$. The empty support retains actual b; if b=0 its normalized ratio lies outside the defined domain. This shared claim states the nonzero condition explicitly and does not resolve the source zero-coefficient definition.

proof_steps.title: Reconstruct linearly from actual current dividends
proof_steps.body_md: For current game h and fixed reference family U, each used nonzero U_S gives $U_S(I_h(S)/U_S)=I_h(S)$. Sum over subsets and apply Möbius reconstruction to obtain h(T). The current h need not equal reference g, and a fixed empirically sparse family is not guaranteed complete for every new input.

en.title: Complex responses and pseudocovariance of real Gaussian kernels
en.overview: Each independent real Gaussian weight $W_t$ maps into $\mathbb C$ by the continuous real linear map $w\mapsto e^{i\theta_t}w$. A finite independent sum remains a real two-dimensional Gaussian. A real W is not a circular complex Gaussian: $\mathbb E(W-\mu)^2=\sigma^2$, rather than zero.

assumptions.body_md: Under the genuine independence reading of the source prose, real weights have laws $\mathcal N(\mu_l,\sigma_l^2)$, kernel elements are independent within a layer, and whole weight vectors are independent across layers. The weaker first-moment reading of Equations (6)–(7) is assessed separately; the required second-moment factorization is not assumed.

definitions.body_md: The output DFT has negative phase, $\widehat f(u,v)=\sum_{m,n}f_{mn}e^{-2\pi i(um/M+vn/N)}$, while the kernel response has positive phase, $T_{dc}^{(uv)}=\sum_{t,s}W_{cts}^{[\mathrm{ker}=d]}e^{2\pi i(ut/M+vs/N)}$.

The finite sums $P_K(z)=\sum_{t<K}z^t$, $R_{uv}=\sum_{t,s<K}e^{2\pi i(ut/M+vs/N)}$, and $\chi_{u^{\prime}v^{\prime}uv}=(MN)^{-1}R_{u-u^{\prime},v-v^{\prime}}$ include equal-coordinate frequencies, with $\chi_{uvuv}=K^2/(MN)$.

$SOM(Z)=\mathbb E|Z|^2$, complex variance $V(Z)=\mathbb E|Z-\mathbb EZ|^2$, and pseudocovariance $C(Z)=\mathbb E(Z-\mathbb EZ)^2$. A real Gaussian embedded in the complex plane has pseudocovariance equal to its real variance.

proof_steps.title: Start with embedded real Gaussians
proof_steps.body_md: Independent real Gaussian weights $W_t$ form a jointly Gaussian real vector. Each $e^{i\theta_t}W_t$ is a real continuous linear map into $\mathbb C$, and independent Gaussian convolution gives a complex Gaussian response. For real $W$, pseudocovariance is $\mathbb E(W-\mu)^2=\sigma^2$; the circular-Gaussian replacement in A.4 is incorrect.

proof_steps.title: Compute the mean and squared-magnitude moment
proof_steps.body_md: Linearity gives $\mathbb ET=\sum_t\mu e^{i\theta_t}=\mu R$. Independence makes distinct centered cross terms zero, and each diagonal variance contributes $\sigma^2$. Hence $V(T)=K^2\sigma^2$ and $SOM(T)=|\mu R|^2+K^2\sigma^2$. These conclusions use actual Gaussian laws and squared-magnitude integrals.

en.overview: Each T_l is a measurable phase sum of its finite real kernel array. Measurable functions of independent layer vectors remain independent, as do their squared magnitudes; the desired moment equality is not assumed.

assumptions.body_md: Under the genuine independence reading of the source prose, real weights have laws $\mathcal N(\mu_l,\sigma_l^2)$, kernel elements are independent within a layer, and whole weight vectors are independent across layers. The weaker first-moment reading of Equations (6)–(7) is assessed separately; the required second-moment factorization is not assumed.

The source assumes C_l=1. The ordinary logarithm formula applies where every moment factor is positive. Standard nondegenerate Gaussian variances σ_l²>0 and K>0 ensure this; degenerate zero-variance cases are explained separately.

definitions.body_md: The output DFT has negative phase, $\widehat f(u,v)=\sum_{m,n}f_{mn}e^{-2\pi i(um/M+vn/N)}$, while the kernel response has positive phase, $T_{dc}^{(uv)}=\sum_{t,s}W_{cts}^{[\mathrm{ker}=d]}e^{2\pi i(ut/M+vs/N)}$.

Keep $\mathbb T^{(uv)(b:a)}=T^{(b,uv)}\cdots T^{(a,uv)}$ in its original order, with empty layer products equal to identity maps, and $\delta_{uv}=1_{\{u=v=0\}}$. Retain spatial biases $b^{(l)}$; spectral bias acts only at DC and carries $MN$.

$SOM(Z)=\mathbb E|Z|^2$, complex variance $V(Z)=\mathbb E|Z-\mathbb EZ|^2$, and pseudocovariance $C(Z)=\mathbb E(Z-\mathbb EZ)^2$. A real Gaussian embedded in the complex plane has pseudocovariance equal to its real variance.

The finite sums $P_K(z)=\sum_{t<K}z^t$, $R_{uv}=\sum_{t,s<K}e^{2\pi i(ut/M+vs/N)}$, and $\chi_{u^{\prime}v^{\prime}uv}=(MN)^{-1}R_{u-u^{\prime},v-v^{\prime}}$ include equal-coordinate frequencies, with $\chi_{uvuv}=K^2/(MN)$.

proof_steps.title: Derive response independence from actual layer arrays
proof_steps.body_md: Each $T_l$ is a measurable phase sum of its finite real kernel array. Measurable maps preserve independence of whole layer vectors, giving independent families $T_l$ and $|T_l|^2$. The complex Bochner product integral gives $\mathbb E\prod_lT_l=\prod_l\mathbb ET_l=\prod_l(\mu_lR_{uv})$. All Gaussian means are derived from actual laws rather than assuming the desired product identity.

proof_steps.title: Integrate the actual squared-magnitude product
proof_steps.body_md: Apply the shared independent-product integral theorem to the real variables $|T_l|^2$, then substitute the actual Gaussian kernel moments. The empty layer product is one; the finite-depth result needs neither asymptotics nor the law of large numbers.

proof_steps.title: Expand logs on the positive-moment domain
proof_steps.body_md: First use the declared positive factors $a_l>0$ to apply the ordinary real $\log$ identity: $\log SOM(\mathbb T)=\sum_l\log a_l$. The conditions $K>0$ and $\sigma_l^2>0$ imply $a_l\ge K^2\sigma_l^2>0$ and are sufficient rather than necessary; $\sigma_l^2=0$ with $|\mu_lR|>0$ is also covered. If a factor is zero, ordinary $\log0$ is undefined. The source-domain boundary remains; Lean’s totalized log0 is not used.
